content: For NSCLC with common EGFR sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R), osimertinib is the preferred first-line targeted therapy category 1 recommendation over earlier-generation EGFR-TKIs based on improved CNS activity and overall survival.

In unresectable stage III EGFR-mutated NSCLC, concurrent chemoradiation followed by durvalumab consolidation is standard. EGFR-TKI monotherapy without chemoradiation is not recommended for unresectable stage III disease outside clinical trials.
Upon progression on first- or second-generation EGFR-TKI, re-biopsy or plasma ctDNA testing for T790M is recommended. Osimertinib is preferred for T790M-positive disease.
Recommended dose: 80 mg orally once daily with or without food until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Reduce to 40 mg daily for grade 3 or higher adverse reactions.

Common adverse reactions include diarrhea (58%), rash (58%), dry skin, and nail toxicity. Monitor for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis — withhold osimertinib if ILD is suspected and permanently discontinue if confirmed.

No dose adjustment required for mild to moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance 30 mL/min or greater). Osimertinib has not been studied in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min).

KRAS G12C mutation defines a subset amenable to targeted therapy. Sotorasib or adagrasib may be used in previously treated locally advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC after prior systemic therapy.
For ALK rearrangement-positive metastatic NSCLC, alectinib, brigatinib, or lorlatinib are preferred first-line ALK inhibitor options over crizotinib based on superior efficacy and CNS penetration.

For metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS 50% or greater and no EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations, pembrolizumab monotherapy is a category 1 first-line option. PD-L1 1-49% favors chemo-immunotherapy combination.

Unresectable stage III NSCLC: concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation followed by durvalumab consolidation for up to 12 months is standard of care (PACIFIC regimen). ECOG 0-1 required for consolidation immunotherapy.

On progression after osimertinib, repeat biopsy for resistance mechanisms (C797S, MET amplification, histologic transformation). Amivantamab-based regimens may be considered for EGFR exon 19 or L858R with acquired resistance mutations.

Amivantamab is indicated for EGFR exon 20 insertion-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC. Premedicate for infusion-related reactions. Common AEs: rash, paronychia, infusion reactions, and hypomagnesemia.

During EGFR-TKI therapy, assess response with CT chest/abdomen every 6-12 weeks for first 2 years. Rising ctDNA may precede radiographic progression — consider tissue re-biopsy at progression for resistance profiling.

Neoadjuvant targeted therapy for resectable EGFR-mutated NSCLC remains investigational but emerging trial data (NeoADAURA) support neoadjuvant osimertinib in stage II-IIIB resectable disease with major pathologic response rates exceeding historical chemotherapy.

Immune-mediated adverse reactions include colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, and endocrinopathies. Permanently discontinue for grade 3-4 colitis. Do not use pembrolizumab in patients with active autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppression.
